name: MSSQL Linked Server Chain Abuse (PowerUpSQL)
description: Enumerate and abuse MSSQL linked server chains to execute OS commands on remote SQL servers, potentially crossing domain trust boundaries.

examples.label: Find all SQL servers in domain
Add local admin via MSSQL
examples.command: Invoke-SQLOSCmd -Instance 10.10.10.20 -Command 'net user hacker Password123! /add && net localgroup administrators hacker /add'

recommended.note: MSSQL links may cross trust boundaries
Lateral movement to MSSQL host after RCE

notes: xp_cmdshell must be enabled or you need sa/sysadmin. Links often use over-privileged service accounts. sa accounts should not exist in production.

defense.why_it_works: MSSQL Server supports linked server connections that allow one SQL instance to query another. These links authenticate using either pre-configured credentials or the SQL server service account's Windows token. PowerUpSQL's Get-SQLServerLinkCrawl walks the chain of linked servers and can execute queries (and OS commands via xp_cmdshell) on each hop — often with escalating privileges across trust boundaries.
defense.prerequisites: SQL access to at least one MSSQL instance (often via sysadmin or public role). PowerUpSQL module. MSSQL linked servers configured with high-privilege credentials. xp_cmdshell enabled or enableable (sa/sysadmin required).
defense.impact: T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares + T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services. Code execution on multiple SQL servers via linked server chain. If any hop has sysadmin rights via the link, xp_cmdshell gives OS command execution — potentially on servers across network segments or domains.
defense.detection:
Event 4624 on target SQL servers showing the linking service account authenticating. SQL Server audit log: linked server queries traversing the chain (especially EXECUTE AT and OPENQUERY across servers). Event 4688: xp_cmdshell child process spawned (cmd.exe or powershell.exe as child of sqlservr.exe). SIEM: recursive linked server queries from a single session. PowerUpSQL User-Agent if using web-delivery.
Logon via RDP or WMI by user account followed by uncommon command execution, file manipulation, or lateral network connections (DET0269/AN0750).
SSH session from new source IP followed by interactive shell, privilege escalation (sudo, su), and outbound lateral connection (AN0751).
Remote login via ARD or SSH followed by screensharingd activity or modification of TCC-protected files (AN0752).
Cloud bastion or VM console session followed by commands initiating outbound SSH/RDP to other environments (AN0753).
vSphere API logins or SSH to ESXi followed by unauthorized shell commands or lateral remote logins from the ESXi host (AN0754).
defense.artifacts: SQL audit log: EXECUTE AT LinkedServer from unusual source | Event 4688: cmd.exe/powershell.exe child of sqlservr.exe | Event 4624: SQL service account logon from unexpected host | Sysmon Event 1: sqlservr.exe spawning cmd.exe
defense.prevention:
Audit linked servers: SELECT * FROM sys.servers WHERE is_linked = 1. Remove unnecessary linked servers. Use least-privilege credentials for links (no sysadmin). Disable xp_cmdshell: EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 0; RECONFIGURE. Enable SQL Server Audit to log linked server queries and xp_cmdshell invocations. Segment SQL servers to prevent cross-domain links.
Audit: Scan systems, permissions, insecure configurations to identify weaknesses.
Disable or Remove Feature or Program: Disable unnecessary remote service connection types; enable ESXi lockdown mode requiring vCenter management.
Limit Access to Resource Over Network: Prevent unnecessary remote access to file shares, hypervisors, and sensitive systems; use network concentrators and RDP gateways.
Multi-factor Authentication: Use MFA on remote service logons where possible.
Password Policies: Do not reuse local administrator passwords across systems; ensure complexity and uniqueness.
User Account Management: Limit accounts that may use remote services; limit high-risk account permissions; configure SSH to restrict programs users can run.
defense.evasion: Use OPENQUERY instead of EXECUTE AT (different audit events). Traverse links via legitimate queries to disguise enumeration. Use Windows Auth links (harder to audit than SQL Auth links).
defense.misconfiguration: Linked servers configured with SA or sysadmin credentials. xp_cmdshell enabled. Links span domains with overprivileged accounts. No SQL audit enabled. SQL service account has domain admin rights.

variations.label: Run OS command across the link chain
